heroHeadline: Germany Opens National Drone-Defence Centre as NATO Flies High-End Air Package Near Kaliningrad
heroSubtitle: Two weeks after an explosive-laden drone was found beside a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig/Halle Airport, Germany opened a national drone-security research centre in Cochstedt on August 18 — the same day NATO flew an estimated 25-50 aircraft air-defence package, including a U.S. EA-37B electronic-warfare jet, over Poland and the Baltic near Russia's Kaliningrad exclave. The moves follow a 152-day wave of Russian drone and aircraft incursions that has produced seven NATO shootdowns/intercepts across Estonia, Latvia, and Romania, an apartment-block strike in Galați, and the collapse of Latvia's government.
footerNote: Data sourced from official NATO/SHAPE and member-state defense ministry statements, major outlets, and institutional analyses.
